United Kingdom.text: Became the world's first industrialised country.
United Kingdom.evidence: The UK became the first industrialised country and was the world's foremost power for the majority of the 19th and early 20th centuries, particularly during the Pax Britannica between 1815 and 1914.

Germany.text: It is the world's third-largest exporter and, at the same time, its third-largest importer.
Germany.evidence: As a major force in several industrial, scientific and technological sectors, Germany is both the world's third-largest exporter and third-largest importer.

Brazil.text: Borders every other country and territory in South America except Ecuador and Chile.
Brazil.evidence: Covering roughly half of South America's land area, it borders all other countries and territories on the continent except Ecuador and Chile.

France.text: Five of its 18 regions are overseas, including French Guiana in South America.
France.evidence: Its overseas regions and territories include French Guiana in South America, Saint Pierre and Miquelon in the North Atlantic, the French West Indies, and many islands in Oceania and the Indian Ocean. ... Its 18 integral regions—five of which are overseas—span a combined area of 632,702 km2 (244,288 sq mi), with a total population estimated at over 69.1 million in 2026.

Netherlands.text: The name literally means "lower countries", and 26% of the land is below sea level.
Netherlands.evidence: Netherlands literally means "lower countries", in reference to its low elevation and flat topography, 26% of which is below sea level.

Finland.text: Mostly covered by boreal forest, with over 180,000 recorded lakes.
Finland.evidence: Its land is predominantly covered by boreal forest, with over 180,000 recorded lakes.

Australia.text: Its mainland is the world's flattest and driest inhabited continent.
Australia.evidence: It has a land area of 7,688,287 km2 (2,968,464 sq mi), making it the sixth-largest country in the world, and is the world's flattest and driest inhabited continent.

Italy.text: Besides the peninsula, the country takes in nearly 800 islands, notably Sicily and Sardinia.
Italy.evidence: It consists of a peninsula, which extends into the Mediterranean Sea, with the Alps on its northern land border, as well as nearly 800 islands, notably Sicily and Sardinia.

Austria.text: Declared its perpetual neutrality in 1955, after a decade of Allied occupation.
Austria.evidence: After its liberation in 1945 and a decade of Allied occupation, the country regained its sovereignty and declared its perpetual neutrality in 1955.

Argentina.text: Claims sovereignty over the Falkland Islands, South Georgia and a part of Antarctica.
Argentina.evidence: Argentina claims sovereignty over the Falkland Islands, South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands, the Southern Patagonian Ice Field, and a part of Antarctica.
